scenarios.name: Hero Section Display
scenarios.description: Verify the hero section displays product name, tagline, value proposition, and prominent call-to-action buttons as required by REQ-1 and REQ-4

steps.description: Navigate to the root URL of the MirDB landing page
steps.context: Page should load within 2 seconds (NFR-1)

steps.description: Check that the hero section contains product name, logo, tagline about persistent key-value store with memcached compatibility, and value proposition
steps.context: Hero section should be visible above the fold without scrolling

steps.description: Confirm presence of primary CTA (Get Started/View Documentation) and secondary CTA (GitHub Repository) buttons
steps.context: CTAs should be accessible without scrolling per REQ-4

test_cases.expected: Product name 'MirDB' is displayed prominently
Tagline containing 'persistent key-value store' and 'memcached' is displayed
Value proposition text (2-3 sentences) explaining MirDB benefits is present
Primary CTA button with text 'Get Started' or 'View Documentation' is visible
Secondary CTA button linking to GitHub repository is visible
User is navigated to documentation page
User is navigated to MirDB GitHub repository in new tab

scenarios.name: Features Section Display
scenarios.description: Verify the features section displays three primary feature cards highlighting memcached compatibility, persistence, and LSM architecture as required by REQ-2

steps.description: Scroll to the features section of the landing page
steps.context: Features section should be easily discoverable below the hero

steps.description: Confirm three feature cards are displayed: Memcached Compatible, Persistent Storage, High Performance
steps.context: Each card should have icon, title, and brief description

steps.description: Check that each feature card contains meaningful description of the benefit
steps.context: Descriptions should be concise and highlight user benefits

test_cases.expected: Memcached Compatible feature card is displayed with icon, title, and description mentioning 'existing memcached clients'
Persistent Storage feature card is displayed with icon, title, and description mentioning 'SSTable storage' or 'data survives restarts'
High Performance feature card is displayed with icon, title, and description mentioning 'LSM tree' or 'async I/O'
Each feature card contains a visual icon element

test_cases.input: Render features section on desktop viewport
test_cases.expected: Feature cards are arranged horizontally in a row

scenarios.name: Quick Start Code Section
scenarios.description: Verify the quick-start section displays a code snippet showing basic MirDB usage with copy-to-clipboard functionality as required by REQ-3

steps.description: Scroll to the quick-start or getting started section
steps.context: Section should demonstrate basic SET and GET operations

steps.description: Confirm code snippet shows MirDB server startup and basic memcached commands (SET, GET)
steps.context: Code should be syntax-highlighted for readability

steps.description: Click copy button and verify code is copied to clipboard
steps.context: Should provide visual feedback on successful copy

test_cases.expected: Code snippet container is displayed with visible code block
Code snippet contains 'mirdb' or server start command
Code snippet contains 'set' command example
Code snippet contains 'get' command example
Code block has syntax highlighting applied (colored text or appropriate CSS classes)
Copy-to-clipboard button is visible near the code block
Code content is copied to system clipboard
Visual feedback is shown (e.g., button text changes to 'Copied!' or checkmark icon)

scenarios.name: Supported Commands Display
scenarios.description: Verify the page displays supported memcached commands (GET, SET, DELETE, ADD, REPLACE, APPEND, PREPEND) as required by REQ-5

steps.description: Find the section displaying supported memcached commands
steps.context: Commands should be clearly listed for developer reference

steps.description: Confirm all supported commands are displayed: GET, SET, DELETE, ADD, REPLACE, APPEND, PREPEND
steps.context: Per PRD appendix, these are the currently supported commands

test_cases.expected: GET command is listed in supported commands
SET command is listed in supported commands
DELETE command is listed in supported commands
ADD command is listed in supported commands
REPLACE command is listed in supported commands
APPEND command is listed in supported commands
PREPEND command is listed in supported commands

scenarios.name: Configuration Example Display
scenarios.description: Verify the page shows configuration example with default parameters as required by REQ-6

steps.description: Find the section displaying configuration options and defaults
steps.context: Should show TOML configuration format with default values

steps.description: Confirm default configuration values are displayed: Port 12333, Max LSM levels 7, Memtable size 4MB, SSTable max size 100MB, Block size 4KB
steps.context: Values should match PRD appendix defaults

test_cases.expected: Default port 12333 is displayed
Max LSM levels value (7) is displayed
Memtable size (4MB) is displayed
SSTable max size (100MB) is displayed
Block size (4KB) is displayed
Configuration is shown in TOML format or structured table

scenarios.name: MirDB vs Memcached Comparison
scenarios.description: Verify the comparison section positions MirDB advantages vs standard memcached as required by REQ-7

steps.description: Find the comparison table or section comparing MirDB to memcached
steps.context: Comparison should highlight MirDB's persistence advantages

steps.description: Confirm comparison shows: Data Persistence (Yes vs No), Protocol compatibility, Crash Recovery (WAL+SSTable vs None), Async I/O support
steps.context: Content should match PRD comparison table

test_cases.expected: Comparison table or grid is displayed with MirDB and Memcached columns
Data Persistence row shows MirDB as 'Yes' or 'SSTable' and Memcached as 'No' or 'Memory only'
Protocol row shows both support Memcached protocol
Crash Recovery row shows MirDB has WAL + SSTable and Memcached has None
Async I/O row shows MirDB is Tokio-based
MirDB advantages are visually emphasized (highlighting, checkmarks, or color coding)

scenarios.name: Footer Navigation
scenarios.description: Verify the footer contains links to documentation, GitHub, and community resources as required by REQ-9

steps.description: Scroll to the bottom of the page to view the footer
steps.context: Footer should be consistently present at page bottom

steps.description: Confirm presence of Documentation, GitHub, and License links
steps.context: All links should be functional and point to correct destinations

steps.description: Check for project version/status and copyright notice
steps.context: Footer should provide complete reference information

test_cases.expected: Footer element is present at the bottom of the page
Documentation link is present and visible
GitHub link is present and visible
License link is present and visible
Copyright notice is displayed
User is navigated to documentation site
User is navigated to MirDB GitHub repository
User is navigated to license information page or section

scenarios.name: Responsive Design - Mobile
scenarios.description: Verify the page is fully responsive and usable on mobile devices as required by NFR-2

steps.description: Resize browser or use device emulation to mobile viewport (375px width)
steps.context: Testing iPhone SE / small mobile device sizes

steps.description: Confirm all text is readable without horizontal scrolling
steps.context: Text should be appropriately sized for mobile

steps.description: Check that navigation is accessible via mobile-friendly interface (hamburger menu or similar)
steps.context: Navigation should be easy to use on touch devices

steps.description: Confirm all interactive elements are large enough for touch input (min 44x44px)
steps.context: Buttons and links should be easily tappable

test_cases.expected: No horizontal scrollbar appears
Hero section text is fully visible and readable
Feature cards stack vertically
Code snippet section is horizontally scrollable or wrapped appropriately
CTA buttons are full-width or appropriately sized for mobile
All touch targets are at least 44x44 pixels
Page layout adapts appropriately for tablet size

scenarios.name: Accessibility Compliance
scenarios.description: Verify the page meets WCAG 2.1 AA accessibility standards as required by NFR-3

steps.description: Navigate entire page using only keyboard (Tab, Shift+Tab, Enter)
steps.context: All interactive elements should be reachable and usable

steps.description: Verify all text meets WCAG AA contrast ratios (4.5:1 for normal text, 3:1 for large text)
steps.context: Use contrast checker tool

steps.description: Confirm all images have descriptive alt text
steps.context: Alt text should convey image meaning to screen reader users

steps.description: Verify visible focus indicators on all interactive elements
steps.context: Focus state should be clearly visible

test_cases.input: Tab through all interactive elements on page
test_cases.expected: All links, buttons, and form elements are reachable via keyboard

test_cases.input: Check all text elements with contrast analyzer
test_cases.expected: All text meets minimum contrast ratio of 4.5:1 for normal text
All images have non-empty, descriptive alt attributes
Visible focus indicator is displayed (outline, border, or background change)
Proper heading hierarchy (h1, h2, h3) is used throughout the page
Semantic elements (header, nav, main, section, footer) are used appropriately

test_cases.input: Inspect code blocks with screen reader
test_cases.expected: Code snippets are accessible to screen readers (proper ARIA labels or role)
Accessibility score is 90 or higher

scenarios.name: Performance Requirements
scenarios.description: Verify the page meets performance requirements: load time under 2 seconds and page weight under 500KB as required by NFR-1

steps.description: Load page and measure Time to Interactive (TTI) and Largest Contentful Paint (LCP)
steps.context: Using Lighthouse or similar performance tool

steps.description: Check total page size including all assets (HTML, CSS, JS, images, fonts)
steps.context: Target is under 500KB total

steps.description: Confirm images are compressed and CSS/JS is minified
steps.context: Optimization reduces load time and bandwidth

test_cases.input: Load page on standard broadband connection
test_cases.expected: Page loads (DOMContentLoaded) in under 2 seconds
Performance score is 90 or higher
LCP is under 2.5 seconds

test_cases.input: Measure total page weight via DevTools Network tab
test_cases.expected: Total page size is under 500KB
All images are compressed and optimized (WebP or compressed PNG/JPG)
CSS and JavaScript files are minified for production
Images below the fold implement lazy loading
